issues.on_page: Other 13,885,533 (General 3,725,944; Inheritance 1,819,259; Road 222,445; Insurance 5,005,508; Other Governmental 3,112,377)
issues.issue: 27% of governmental receipts are in 'other'. The fund schedules (pp4, 6-10) print what the line is made of: fees of office about 2.9M, inheritance tax 1,744,270, Insurance Fund interfund premiums 5,005,508, lottery 994,361, commissary 507,331, gaming tax 327,882, 911 surcharges 166,774, and more. No single category is more than half, so 'other' with review follows the rules. However, the State line was split from the same schedules and this line was not, so the treatment is inconsistent.

On the p11 department schedule this equals the sum of every 'Misc.' column: General Government 1,500,562 + Public Safety 804,980 + Public Works 167,515 + Public Welfare 104,998 + Culture 37,500 + Public Health 647,741 = 3,263,296. It is a mixed line, and general government is only 46% of it.

The statement (p3) nonmajor Public Safety 1,212,250 minus Drug Court 265,701, Drug Enforcement 7,200, Inmate Welfare 741,022 and Emergency Management 161,000 leaves exactly 37,327. This suggests the statement counts the line as public safety. 'Operating' (no printed function) is defensible.

It is an 'assessment' for spraying done for landowners. Charges for services is defensible, but special assessments is also possible.

This is a one-sided transfer. No fund records a matching transfer in, and the statement (p3) counts the 59,076 as a disbursement (nonmajor transfers out 612,832 vs combining schedule 671,908).
